description: Precise MVP scope for EntrepreneurOS -- what ships first and what does not, across 5 incremental releases from Core Shell to Docs+Memory, for a single founder operating a single business.
provenance_detail: Synthesized from: phase14_6b_eos_preflight.json (product hierarchy, communication chain, UI shell), phase14_6b_eos_onboarding_first_boot_spec.json (25-step onboarding, 4 paths), phase14_6b_eos_ui_ux_aesthetic_canon.json (executive command center aesthetic, design tokens), phase14_6b_eos_communication_delegation_architecture.json (EA->CEO->department routing chain, permission tiers), phase14_6b_eos_portfolio_entity_business_ontology.json (portfolio/entity/business model), phase14_6b_eos_workflow_sop_engine_spec.json (workflow R3 scope), phase14_6b_eos_analytics_kpi_spec.json (per-release analytics build-out), phase14_6b_eos_agent_architecture_spec.json (per-release agent activation), phase14_6b_eos_org_chart_engine_spec.json (department/role/template system), phase14_6b_eos_governance_permissions_model.json (RBAC-first MVP, ABAC deferred), phase14_6b_eos_api_contract_map.json (per-release API surface), phase14_6b_eos_auth_security_truth.json (Clerk target, Beast branch state), phase14_6b_eos_current_implementation_truth.json (GitHub main 202 files, Beast 603 files), phase14_6b_eos_data_ontology.json (22 entity schema), phase14_6b_eos_infrastructure_deployment_map.md (zero production deployment, target architecture), phase14_6b_eos_implementation_debt_register.md (debt inventory across all surfaces), phase14_6b_eos_business_template_library.json (19 business type templates), phase14_6b_eos_business_democratization_doctrine.json (democratization thesis), operator corrections from Phase 14.6B mission brief.

mvp_definition.scope: AI-assisted company command center for one founder, one business -- the minimum product that lets a solo operator sign up, configure a business entity, receive AI-generated operational structure, manage tasks, run workflows, talk to AI agents, and track KPIs from a single executive dashboard.
mvp_definition.constraint: Single-tenant, single-user. One operator, one portfolio, one primary entity. No multi-user roles, no team invites, no enterprise features, no marketplace.
mvp_definition.persona: Solo founder or early-stage operator who wants to run a real business with AI-native infrastructure from day one. Not a side-project hobbyist -- someone building an economic entity that needs structure, accountability, and intelligence.
mvp_definition.value_proposition: EOS replaces the founder's spreadsheet-plus-Notion-plus-Slack patchwork with a single command center where AI agents handle operational work, workflows enforce discipline, and KPIs surface what matters -- all governed by a hierarchy the founder controls.
what_mvp_proves: A single founder can configure and operate a business entirely through EOS
AI agents reduce operational burden measurably (task completion, report generation, workflow drafting)
The executive command center aesthetic creates trust and retention in the target persona
The onboarding flow produces a ready-to-use operating system in under 10 minutes
The platform architecture supports future multi-entity, multi-user, and marketplace expansion without rewrite
what_mvp_does_not_prove: Autonomous agent execution without human oversight

releases.name: Core Shell
releases.scope: Authentication, onboarding, business entity creation, app shell with executive command center layout, settings, home dashboard with KPI strip, CEO agent for morning brief and strategic analysis.
releases.description: R1 is the foundation. The operator can sign up via Clerk, complete the 25-step onboarding flow (simplified to essential steps for R1), create their first business entity, see the executive dashboard with 5 KPIs, and interact with the CEO agent. The app shell (left rail, main workspace, right rail AI, floating AI control) is established. Settings are accessible. This is the minimum viable experience -- the operator sees EOS working and has a reason to come back.

features.name: Clerk authentication
features.description: Sign up, sign in, password reset, Google OAuth via Clerk. Session management delegated to Clerk. ClerkProvider wraps React app, clerkMiddleware() on Express backend.
features.source: Beast feature/company-system branch (already implemented)

features.name: Onboarding flow (R1 subset)
features.description: Streamlined onboarding: account creation (step 1-2), onboarding path selection (step 3), business name and type (step 4), business stage (step 5), industry and model (step 6-7), AI-generated org chart preview (steps 9-11 simplified), initial KPI selection (step 13 simplified), completion and entry to active mode (step 25). Steps 8, 12, 14-24 deferred to later releases.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_onboarding_first_boot_spec.json (25-step spec, R1 activates essential subset)

features.name: Business entity creation and management
features.description: Create a single business entity within a default portfolio. Entity stores name, type, stage, industry, business model. Entity dashboard shows KPI strip. Entity can be edited in settings. Portfolio is auto-created (single portfolio for MVP) -- portfolio management UI deferred.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_portfolio_entity_business_ontology.json

features.name: App shell with executive command center layout
features.description: Left Rail (role-dependent navigation, entity indicator), Main Workspace (content area), Right Rail AI Assistant (persistent chat with CEO agent), Floating AI Control Panel (quick actions). Dark mode default. Finance-grade aesthetic per UI/UX canon. Header with entity name and navigation. Activity feed in sidebar.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_ui_ux_aesthetic_canon.json (shell layout, design tokens, aesthetic direction)

features.name: Home dashboard with KPI strip
features.description: Dashboard displays 5 core KPIs: net_revenue, cash_on_hand, pipeline_value, task_completion_rate, decision_backlog. Basic sparklines. Period comparison (this week vs last week). CEO morning brief summary card. Quick action buttons. No drill-down, no benchmarking in R1.

features.name: CEO agent
features.description: CEO agent is the sole active agent in R1. Provides morning brief, strategic analysis, delegation framework (delegate targets display as 'coming soon' for departments not yet active). Chat interface in Right Rail. CEO agent uses call_with_fallback() via UMH model_router. Risk classification via substrate governance engine.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_agent_architecture_spec.json (R1: ceo_agent only), projections/eos/agents/ceo.py (existing implementation)

features.name: Settings page
features.description: Account settings (profile, password change via Clerk). Business entity settings (name, type, stage, industry editable). App settings (theme toggle dark/light, notification preferences). No governance settings, no agent configuration, no integration management in R1.
features.source: Beast branch settings-page.tsx (partial implementation exists)

features.name: Design token system
features.description: CSS custom properties implementing finance-grade palette. Dark mode primary, light mode secondary. Status colors (green/red/amber/blue/gray). Professional sans-serif typography. Monospace for financial figures. 4px grid spacing. Design tokens loaded from shared config, not hardcoded per component.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_ui_ux_aesthetic_canon.json (design tokens section), Beast design-tokens.ts (partial implementation)

features.name: Task board

releases.name: Workflows
releases.scope: Workflow library, workflow creation (manual + AI-drafted), workflow runner with step-through execution, SOP creation and linking, Finance agent activation, CRM (contacts + deals + pipeline), basic financial tracking.
releases.description: R3 makes EOS process-driven. The operator browses a workflow library, creates custom workflows (or lets AI draft them from a description), runs workflows step-by-step with manual and AI-assisted modes, and links SOPs to workflow steps. CRM goes live with contacts, deals, and a pipeline view. Finance agent tracks revenue and expenses. This release transforms EOS from a task manager into an operational system.

features.name: Workflow library
features.description: Browse, search, and filter workflows. 3 pre-built workflows from existing code (outreach, follow-up, content). 8 template workflows generated during onboarding based on business type. Workflow cards show: name, description, step count, last run date, run count, status (active/draft/archived).
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_workflow_sop_engine_spec.json (R3 scope: library, 3 pre-built, 8 templates)

features.name: Workflow creation and AI drafting
features.description: Manual workflow creation: name, description, add steps (manual/ai_assisted/approval_gate/checkpoint types), set step order, configure step details. AI-assisted creation: operator describes a process in natural language, AI generates a complete workflow definition with steps, approvals, and checkpoints. Operator can edit AI-generated workflows before activating.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_workflow_sop_engine_spec.json (R3: manual definition + AI-generated from description)

features.name: Workflow runner
features.description: Execute a workflow step-by-step. Two modes: manual (operator completes each step) and hybrid (AI handles ai_assisted steps, operator handles manual and approval_gate steps). Step status tracking (pending/active/completed/skipped/failed). Checkpoint steps allow operator to verify before continuing. Run audit trail with timestamps and outcomes per step. Task generation from workflow steps.
features.source: phase14_6b_eos_workflow_sop_engine_spec.json (R3: run view, step-through, manual + hybrid modes, audit trail)

features.name: SOP creation and linking

SOP library browsable independently.

explicit_exclusions.description: MVP creates a single default portfolio for the operator. Multi-portfolio switching, portfolio comparison, and portfolio-level dashboards are excluded. The data model supports multiple portfolios but the UI is single-portfolio.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Single founder, single business constraint. Portfolio intelligence requires multi-entity which requires multi-portfolio. Sequential dependency.

explicit_exclusions.description: The Portfolio Advisor Agent that provides cross-entity strategic recommendations, capital allocation analysis, and entity health scoring. Excluded because MVP is single-entity.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Portfolio Advisor adds value only with multiple entities. Single-founder single-business does not benefit from portfolio-level intelligence.

explicit_exclusions.description: The Universal Business Operating System template marketplace where operators share and sell workflow templates, SOPs, and business configurations. Excluded entirely from MVP.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Marketplace requires multi-operator support, payment infrastructure, template versioning, trust scoring, and community governance. None of these exist in single-user MVP.

explicit_exclusions.description: Agent skill marketplace where skills can be browsed, purchased, installed, rated, and versioned. Skill trust scoring and community contributions.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Same marketplace infrastructure dependency as UBOS templates. Single-user MVP uses built-in skills only.

explicit_exclusions.description: Inviting team members, assigning roles (admin/manager/member/viewer), role-based access control across team members, team-level permissions, activity feeds per team member.
explicit_exclusions.source_module: Role System, Governance and Permissions Model
explicit_exclusions.rationale: MVP is single operator. RBAC for multiple users requires role assignment UI, invitation flow, permission matrix, and team-level governance. All deferred.

explicit_exclusions.description: Attribute-Based Access Control policy engine that evaluates access based on operator attributes, resource attributes, environmental conditions, and composite policies beyond simple role assignment.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: ABAC adds value only with multiple users having different contexts. Single operator does not benefit from attribute-based policy evaluation. The RBAC foundation is designed to be non-breaking when ABAC layers on top.

explicit_exclusions.description: Agents executing at FULLY_AUTONOMOUS level where they independently take actions including HIGH risk without human oversight. All MVP agents operate at SUPERVISED or SEMI_AUTONOMOUS (R4 upgrade).
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Fully autonomous execution requires proven governance, extensive testing, and operator trust built through SUPERVISED and SEMI_AUTONOMOUS experience. Safety-critical -- cannot ship without track record.

explicit_exclusions.description: Workflows triggered automatically by events (new lead, revenue threshold, deadline approaching) or conditions (if deal value > X, if task overdue > 3 days). MVP workflows are manually triggered or agent-initiated.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Requires event bus infrastructure, condition evaluation engine, and reliable scheduling. Each is a significant infrastructure investment beyond MVP scope.

explicit_exclusions.feature: Advanced workflow branching (parallel, split, loop, subprocess)
explicit_exclusions.description: Parallel execution of workflow branches, conditional splits with multiple paths, loop constructs for repeating steps, and subprocess invocation (workflow calling another workflow).
explicit_exclusions.rationale: MVP supports linear step sequences with simple conditional (if/else on step output). Advanced branching requires a workflow execution engine with state machine semantics.

explicit_exclusions.description: SOX compliance workflows, regulatory report generation, data retention policies, configurable audit retention, external auditor access roles, compliance dashboards, multi-region data residency.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Enterprise features require regulatory expertise, formal audit processes, and compliance certification. Fundamentally different from solo-founder MVP.

explicit_exclusions.description: Investment vehicle entities, holding company entities, real estate entities, stock portfolio entities, asset tracking with appreciation/depreciation, portfolio allocation optimization, return metrics.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: MVP supports business entities only (the operator's company). Investment and asset entity types require dedicated agents (investment_analyst, asset_manager, property_manager), different KPI frameworks, and regulatory compliance surfaces.

explicit_exclusions.feature: Additional department agents (Admin, Research, Content, Automation, Investment Analyst, Asset Manager, Property Manager)
explicit_exclusions.description: Seven department agents beyond the 11 core agents. Each serves specialized entity types or organizational maturity stages not relevant to solo-founder MVP.
explicit_exclusions.source_module: Agent Architecture, Communication and Delegation Architecture
explicit_exclusions.target_release: Post-MVP (triggered by entity type support or organizational growth)
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Admin requires team. Research handled by existing agents' browser skills. Content handled by Marketing for solo founder. Automation handled by Operations at early stage. Investment/Asset/Property require their entity types.

explicit_exclusions.description: System autonomously refines workflows based on run pattern analysis, detects inefficiencies, suggests step reordering, and auto-optimizes execution paths.
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Requires significant historical workflow run data, pattern detection infrastructure, and proven optimization algorithms. Cannot ship meaningfully without months of run data.

explicit_exclusions.description: Comparing operator's KPIs against industry benchmarks (static data sets) and anonymized peer comparisons (dynamic benchmarking requiring multi-operator data).
explicit_exclusions.target_release: R5 includes basic static benchmarks; dynamic deferred to post-MVP multi-operator
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Static benchmarks are a data acquisition problem (sourcing reliable benchmark data). Dynamic benchmarking requires aggregated anonymized data from multiple operators, which is impossible with single-user MVP.

prerequisite_decisions.decision: Beast branch promotion as canonical codebase
prerequisite_decisions.description: Beast feature/company-system branch (603 files, Clerk auth, company system, portfolio management) is promoted over GitHub main (202 files, stale Passport.js, Replit Agent code). This means: merge Beast into main, deprecate stale main code, resolve the 401-file divergence.
prerequisite_decisions.resolution: Beast is the promotion candidate. Phase 14.5 convergence plan and Phase 14.6B current implementation truth both confirm Beast as canonical.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: R1 development starts from Beast branch codebase, not GitHub main.

prerequisite_decisions.description: Where does the EOS React+Express application deploy? Options: Fly.io (aligned with cockpit), Vercel (frontend) + Fly.io (backend), Railway, Render, self-hosted on VPS.
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: Fly.io for both frontend and backend (aligned with UMH cockpit deployment, Dockerfile already exists as a pattern). Vercel for frontend + Fly.io for backend is a reasonable alternative if CDN performance matters.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: Determines CI/CD pipeline design, Docker vs serverless build, and deployment automation in R1.

prerequisite_decisions.description: Does EOS use the same Neon project as UMH substrate, or a separate Neon project? Shared project means shared connection limits and billing. Separate project means independent scaling but additional management.
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: Separate Neon project for EOS SaaS data (users, entities, CRM, workflows). UMH substrate data stays in the existing Neon project. EOS backend queries both via connection strings. This isolates SaaS data lifecycle from substrate data lifecycle.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: Schema migration strategy, connection pooling, RLS policy scope, and billing.

prerequisite_decisions.description: How does the EOS TypeScript backend call UMH Python substrate for agent intelligence, governance, and execution? Options: (A) Direct Python bridge (stdin/stdout JSON protocol, already exists at transports/api/), (B) HTTP API calls to UMH cockpit endpoints, (C) Hybrid -- Python bridge for latency-sensitive, HTTP for async.
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: HTTP API calls to UMH substrate endpoints (transports/api/http/). The cockpit already exposes organism, governance, execution, chat, and memory endpoints. EOS backend is a client of UMH HTTP API. No Python bridge needed -- keep the boundary clean.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: R1 architecture: determines whether EOS backend spawns Python processes or makes HTTP calls. Affects latency, error handling, and deployment coupling.

prerequisite_decisions.description: Which Clerk plan supports the features needed? Free tier has limits on MAU, organizations, and social connections. Pro tier removes most limits. What OAuth providers beyond Google?
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: Start with Clerk Free tier (10,000 MAU, sufficient for solo founder + early users). Upgrade to Pro when multi-user features ship. Google OAuth only for R1. GitHub OAuth optional for developer-persona operators.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: Cost, OAuth provider availability, organization feature access.

prerequisite_decisions.description: What domain serves the EOS application? Options: app.entrepreneuros.com, eos.lyfe.institute, app.ostholdings.com, or subdomain of existing property.
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: app.entrepreneuros.com -- branded, memorable, product-specific. Keep separate from UMH cockpit domain (universalmetaharness.tech).
prerequisite_decisions.impact: DNS configuration, Clerk redirect URLs, SSL certificates, and brand consistency.

prerequisite_decisions.description: The full onboarding spec has 25 steps. R1 needs a subset that gets the operator to a usable state quickly. Which steps are essential for R1 and which defer to later releases?
prerequisite_decisions.resolution: R1 essential steps: 1-2 (account), 3 (path), 4 (name/type), 5 (stage), 6-7 (industry/model), 9-11 simplified (org chart preview), 13 simplified (KPI selection), 25 (completion). Steps 8, 12, 14-24 defer. Detailed in R1-F02 above.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: Onboarding completion time, first-time user experience quality.

prerequisite_decisions.description: Beast branch has 6 schema tables (users, agents, tasks, messages, integrations, notifications). UMH platform layer has 14 RLS-enabled tables (users, orgs, members, approvals + more). Target schema has 22 entities. How to reconcile?
prerequisite_decisions.recommendation: Fresh Drizzle migration from Beast schema as base, adding UMH platform tables (orgs, members, approvals). Do not attempt to merge conflicting schemas -- generate a new migration that produces the R1 target schema. UMH substrate keeps its own schema separately.
prerequisite_decisions.impact: R1 schema migration strategy, data model foundation for all subsequent releases.

frontend.state_management: TanStack Query (server state) + React Context (local state)
frontend.design_tokens: CSS custom properties loaded from shared design-tokens.ts

backend.framework: Express 4 (Beast branch) or Hono (UMH platform layer) -- to be reconciled
backend.middleware: Clerk auth middleware, org context middleware, error handler, validation middleware

database.rls: Row-Level Security policies per org (org_id scoping)
database.connection: Neon serverless driver (@neondatabase/serverless) + postgres.js for migrations

auth.organizations: Clerk Organizations for org context (maps to EOS portfolio/entity)
auth.oauth: Google OAuth (via Clerk). GitHub OAuth optional.

ai.embeddings: OpenAI ada-002 or Gemini embedding (for knowledge base semantic search in R5)

deployment.containerization: Docker (multi-stage build: build frontend, serve via Node.js Express)
deployment.environments: staging + production (staging shares Neon branch, production uses main branch)

infrastructure_notes: Beast branch Express backend and UMH Hono backend are separate servers. EOS SaaS backend (Express) calls UMH HTTP API (Hono) for substrate functionality.
No monorepo needed -- EOS SaaS lives in its own repo (antonyfmunoz/EntrepreneurOS). UMH substrate stays in /opt/OS.
Python bridges (transports/api/) are available as fallback if HTTP API latency is unacceptable for agent chat, but HTTP is the recommended path.
Clerk handles all session/auth complexity -- no custom JWT implementation needed.
PostHog is already integrated in Beast branch -- no new analytics setup required.

success_criteria.measurement: PostHog timing: sign-up event to first dashboard render with data

success_criteria.target: Operator opens EOS at least once per business day within first 2 weeks
success_criteria.measurement: PostHog daily active user tracking (session start events)

success_criteria.target: >5 tasks created and >3 tasks completed per week by operator + agents combined
success_criteria.measurement: DB query: tasks created/completed per week per entity

success_criteria.target: >70% of CEO-delegated tasks completed by department agents without operator re-intervention
success_criteria.measurement: DB query: delegated tasks where final status = done without operator reassignment

success_criteria.target: >3 workflows actively run per week by end of first month on R3
success_criteria.measurement: DB query: workflow_runs created per week

success_criteria.target: >10 copilot interactions per day (chat messages, recommendations acted on, workflows created via NL)
success_criteria.measurement: DB query: ai_messages + recommendation actions per day

success_criteria.target: >50 knowledge entries auto-created within first month on R5
success_criteria.measurement: DB query: knowledge_entries created per month

success_criteria.target: EA Agent correctly routes >90% of operator messages to the appropriate downstream agent without mis-routing
success_criteria.measurement: Manual QA + automated routing accuracy test suite

success_criteria.target: All pages load in <2 seconds on initial load, <500ms on subsequent navigation
success_criteria.measurement: Lighthouse performance score + PostHog page timing

success_criteria.target: Operator continues using EOS after 30 days (measured by session activity in week 4-5)
success_criteria.measurement: PostHog cohort: users who signed up week 1, still active week 4-5

success_criteria.target: No data loss events across all releases. All CRUD operations are durable, all agent actions are logged, all workflow runs have complete audit trails.
success_criteria.measurement: Automated integrity checks: orphaned records, missing audit entries, inconsistent state counts

release_timeline_summary.note: Estimates assume single developer + AI agent pair. Parallelization with additional developers could compress timeline significantly. Estimates include testing, deployment, and stabilization time per release.

schema_progression.description: How the database schema grows across releases. Each release adds tables incrementally. No destructive migrations.

agent_activation_progression.description: Which agents are active in each release. Progressive activation builds operator trust and avoids overwhelming with too many agents at once.

r1.note: CEO agent is the sole AI presence. Establishes the agent interaction pattern.

r2.note: First delegation chain: CEO -> Sales. Operator sees work flowing through hierarchy.

r3.note: Financial intelligence added. Three agents covering strategy, revenue, and expenses.

r4.note: Full operational coverage for solo founder. Six agents handling core business functions.

r5.note: Complete agent set. EA Agent completes the canonical routing chain. All departments staffed.

risk_register.risk: Beast branch promotion creates merge conflicts with UMH substrate changes
risk_register.mitigation: Promote Beast as new main immediately. Do not attempt incremental merge. Fresh start with Beast codebase, then integrate UMH platform layer additions.

risk_register.risk: Clerk free tier hits MAU limit before revenue
risk_register.mitigation: 10,000 MAU is generous for pre-revenue. Monitor usage. Budget for Pro tier ($25/month) as needed.

risk_register.risk: UMH HTTP API latency makes agent chat feel slow
risk_register.mitigation: Target <3s for agent response in chat. If UMH API adds >1s overhead, consider co-locating EOS backend with UMH on same Fly.io region, or fall back to Python bridge for chat-specific calls.

risk_register.risk: Schema migrations break existing UMH data
risk_register.mitigation: Use separate Neon project for EOS SaaS data (PRE-DEC-03). EOS schema never touches substrate schema. Connection strings are independent.

risk_register.risk: Single developer bottleneck makes 28-38 week timeline unachievable
risk_register.mitigation: R1 and R2 are the critical path. If R1 takes >6 weeks, re-evaluate scope. AI agent pair (Claude Code) handles significant implementation volume. Consider contracting for frontend work if backend is blocked.

risk_register.risk: Agent quality (hallucination, incorrect delegation, wrong risk classification) erodes operator trust
risk_register.mitigation: All agents ship at SUPERVISED autonomy by default. Every agent action logged. Governance engine uses deterministic risk classification (not LLM-based). Operator can always override. Quality scoring tracks agent accuracy over time.
